title: Nakhon Si Thammarat to Surat Thani 2026: Ai Khai & Cheow Lan
metaDesc: A DIY cross-province trip through Nakhon Si Thammarat and Surat Thani, Thailand: pray to Ai Khai at Wat Chedi in Sichon, stop at a seaside cafe, then sleep on a floating raft house on Cheow Lan Lake (Thailand's Guilin). With routes, timing, rough prices, and tips for making your wish.
keywords: Ai Khai Wat Chedi, Nakhon Si Thammarat travel, Cheow Lan Lake, Nakhon Surat Thani itinerary, Ai Khai to Cheow Lan, Sichon Khanom
h1:
Pray to Ai Khai, Then Sleep on a Raft at Cheow Lan
A Cross-Province Trip: Nakhon Si Thammarat to Surat Thani
intro: This trip puts faith and nature in the same itinerary. Start by going to pray to Ai Khai at Wat Chedi in Sichon, the temple that people from all over southern Thailand visit to make their wishes, then drive a few more hours across into Surat Thani to sleep on a floating raft house at Cheow Lan Lake, the place people call Thailand's Guilin. We've laid it out as a 3-day, 2-night plan with routes, timing, rough prices, and the stops along the way, so you can plan it yourself without guessing.
chips: 🙏 Pray to Ai Khai at Wat Chedi
🛶 Sleep on a raft at Cheow Lan

blocks.html: Nakhon Si Thammarat and Surat Thani sit right next to each other, and the drive from Sichon across to Ban Ta Khun doesn't take long, so it's easy to pair the two provinces' most popular spots into one trip. On the Nakhon side there's Ai Khai at Wat Chedi, the temple boy that lottery-and-luck believers across the country turn to for guidance. On the Surat side there's Cheow Lan Lake, where limestone peaks rise out of emerald-green water, earning it the nickname Thailand's Guilin. This plan suits people driving themselves, and it works out best if you go as a group or a family.

blocks.text: Trip overview: why pair these two places

blocks.html: The main route is Highway 401, which runs along the coast from Nakhon Si Thammarat through Sichon and Khanom into Surat Thani, all the way to Ban Ta Khun, the gateway to Cheow Lan Lake. It's the same single road that strings together Wat Ai Khai, the seaside cafes, and the dam, so you don't have to double back.

items: Day 1 — Head into Nakhon Si Thammarat city, visit Phra That, eat southern food, spend a night in town
Day 2 — Drive north to Sichon, pray to Ai Khai at Wat Chedi, stop at a seaside cafe, then cross into Surat and spend your first night on a raft at Cheow Lan
Day 3 — Watch the morning mist over the lake, take a boat ride for photos, then drive back
Rough distances — Nakhon Si Thammarat city to Sichon is about 65 km; Sichon to the Ratchaprapha Dam pier is about 110–130 km, around 2–2.5 hours of steady driving

blocks.title: Who this plan suits
blocks.html: It suits people driving themselves or renting a car with a driver, because public transport between Sichon and Ban Ta Khun is hard to connect. If you don't have a car, it's easier to fly or take a coach to Surat Thani, then buy a separate dam tour package.

blocks.text: Ai Khai at Wat Chedi: how to pray and how to make a wish

blocks.html: Wat Chedi is in Chalong subdistrict, Sichon district, Nakhon Si Thammarat, open for prayer roughly 6 a.m.–8 p.m. every day. This is the home of Ai Khai, a wooden figure of a temple boy whom people believe grants what you ask for, especially when it comes to trade, luck, and work. It's already busy on weekdays; weekends and long holidays get extremely packed, so leave extra time for parking and queuing.

items: Popular offerings — Firecrackers, plaster rooster sets, red soda, and rooster figurines. Stalls selling offering kits line the front of the temple, so you can buy them on the spot
How to make a wish — Light incense, state your name and address, then ask for what you want and say what you'll offer in return if it comes true. Most people pledge firecrackers or a rooster set

Fulfilling the wish — If you get what you asked for, you have to come back and follow through on what you pledged. There's a spot inside the temple to set off firecrackers, and the sound goes off all day long
Souvenirs out front — There's plenty of Nakhon food and gifts for sale, from snacks to fruit to amulets, so you can shop before you leave

blocks.title: Avoiding the crowds
blocks.html: If you want to pray without being shoulder to shoulder, go early, around 7–8 a.m., when there are still few people and the sun isn't harsh, and parking is easier to find. Lottery draw days (the 1st and 16th) and the days leading up to them get especially packed.

blocks.text: Stops between Sichon and Khanom before crossing provinces

blocks.html: Once you leave Wat Chedi, there's no need to rush off. The Sichon–Khanom stretch is a coastal belt with several beachside cafes and good southern restaurants, so you can refuel before the long drive to the dam. The prices below are approximate, and you should double-check each place's opening days, since some have a regular weekly closing day.

items.name: Hin Ngam Beach, Sichon
items.blurb: Rows of smooth round stones are the signature of Sichon. The water is clear and the atmosphere is quieter than the famous beaches, making it a good place to stop, take photos, and stretch your legs after the temple before a long drive.

items.name: Sea Circle Cafe, Sichon
items.blurb: A seaside cafe surrounded by coconut palms where you can sip coffee with a long view of the sea. Plenty of photo spots, and a good place to rest your legs before driving on.

items.name: Ko Ton, Sichon
items.blurb: An old-school spot that Sichon locals recommend. The standout is Ko Ton's tender stewed pork leg, eaten with hot steamed rice. It genuinely fills you up at local prices, making it a solid lunch before you carry on.

items.name: Luca Beach Club, Sichon
items.blurb: A beachfront restaurant and cafe serving southern Thai food, seafood, and fusion dishes. There are cakes and seaside photo corners, good for anyone who wants to linger.

items.name: Noen Thewada Viewpoint, Khanom
items.blurb: A green grassy hill by the sea looking out over the curve of Khanom Bay. If you turn off to Khanom for a bit, you get a wide, pretty view that's good for late-afternoon photos, though it's a slight detour from the main route.
items.price: Free entry (some spots charge for parking)

items.name: Saeng Daet Cafe & Craft
items.blurb: A small cafe at the mouth of the Surat–Nakhon road, right on the way through, so it's good for a coffee top-up before the long drive to the dam. Open roughly 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m., closed Wednesdays.

blocks.text: Crossing into Surat: what is Cheow Lan Lake?

blocks.html: Once you cross into Surat Thani, the destination is the Ratchaprapha Dam pier in Ban Ta Khun. This dam holds back the Khlong Saeng river, creating a large lake inside Khao Sok National Park. The old limestone peaks became hundreds of islands rising out of the water, shaped like China's Guilin. The spot people photograph most is Khao Sam Kloe, the three-peaked mountain that's the signature image of the place. The real charm is taking a longtail boat in to sleep on a raft house in the middle of the water, then waking up early, opening your door, and finding mist drifting over the lake.

items: Location — Ratchaprapha Dam pier, Ban Ta Khun, Surat Thani, about 90 km from Surat city, then turning off Highway 401 for another 12–14 km
Khao Sok park entry fee — Around 100 THB for Thai adults, around 50 THB for children (foreigners pay more)
Best season — The deep-green water and morning mist are most beautiful in late rainy to early cool season, around November to February
Phone signal — In the middle of the lake the signal is weak to nonexistent, so charge your devices fully before getting on the raft

blocks.html: Most first-timers find it easier to buy a tour package for an overnight stay than to book it themselves, because chartering a longtail boat on your own is expensive. A typical 2-day, 1-night tour starts at around 3,000–3,800 THB per person and includes transfers from the pier, the tour boat, raft accommodation, several meals, life jackets, and insurance. Local operators people use often include Phromthong Yai Tour, Cheow Lan Holiday, and Guilin Lake, and most are contacted by Facebook or by phone in advance.

blocks.title: Straight talk about hidden costs
blocks.html: Some caves have an extra entry or activity fee that isn't included in the main package, like Coral Cave at around 400 THB/person and Nam Talu Cave at around 900 THB/person. Ask clearly when you book what the price covers so you aren't surprised on the day, and note there are no ATMs in the middle of the lake, so bring enough cash.

blocks.text: Activities on the lake: what can you do once you're there?

items.name: Boat ride to Khao Sam Kloe
items.blurb: The highlight every tour takes you to. The boat runs past the three-peaked limestone mountain, the signature photo spot here, at its best in the early morning while there's still mist.

items.name: Kayaking
items.blurb: Many rafts have free kayaks to borrow. Paddle around the raft in the morning or evening; it's quiet and gets you close to rock faces the motorboats can't reach.

items.name: Nam Talu Cave
items.blurb: A short hike, then wading into a cave with a stream running through it. Exciting and beautiful, but you have to wade, and some sections are deep, so check the weather first.

items.name: Swimming off the raft
items.blurb: You can jump straight in off the raft into clear green water; life jackets are provided. Kids love it most, but you always have to wear a life jacket because the water is deep.

items: Cash — Both the offering kits at the temple and the activity fees at the dam run mostly on cash, and there are no ATMs in the middle of the lake
Shoes that can get wet — There's wading and cave-walking at the dam, so strap-on sandals or old sneakers beat slippery flip-flops
A dry bag — To protect your phone, camera, and power bank, since almost everything at the dam gets wet
Fill up before Ban Ta Khun — Petrol stations are sparse near the dam, so fill the tank back in Sichon or in Surat city
Plan around the signal — Tell people at home in advance that you'll be out of contact while you're at the dam
A light jacket — Early mornings on the water are colder than you'd expect, especially in the cool season

faq.q: What do you need to prepare to pray to Ai Khai at Wat Chedi?
faq.a: Bring cash to buy offering kits out front; the popular ones are firecrackers, plaster rooster sets, and red soda. To make a wish, light incense and state your name, address, and what you're asking for, and pledge what you'll offer if it comes true. The temple is open roughly 6 a.m.–8 p.m. every day, and if you want to avoid the crowds, go early in the morning.

faq.q: How far is it from Wat Ai Khai to Cheow Lan Lake, and how long is the drive?
faq.a: From Sichon district to the Ratchaprapha Dam pier at Ban Ta Khun is about 110–130 km, around 2–2.5 hours of steady driving, using Highway 401 as the main road. It's the same single road that passes through Sichon and Khanom into Surat Thani.

faq.q: Do you need your own car for this trip?
faq.a: It's most convenient with your own car or a rental, because public transport between Sichon and Ban Ta Khun is hard to connect. If you don't have a car, it's best to arrive in Surat and buy a separate Cheow Lan Lake tour package, and do Ai Khai as a separate day trip from Nakhon city.

faq.q: For Cheow Lan Lake, should you book a tour or book a raft yourself?
faq.a: If it's your first time or you're a small group, a 2-day, 1-night tour package is better value and more convenient, since it includes the boat, accommodation, meals, and activities, starting at around 3,000–3,800 THB per person. Booking a park raft yourself is cheaper but you have to arrange the boat on your own, which suits experienced travelers going in a larger group.

faq.q: How many days is right for this trip?
faq.a: 3 days and 2 nights is about right: the first day around Nakhon city, the second day praying to Ai Khai and crossing over to sleep on a raft, the third day watching the morning mist before heading back. If you're short on time you can cut the night in town and start straight at Sichon, but you'd have to leave very early.
